claims.claim: Cummins bridges electricity/fuel inputs to reliable distributed and standby power for data centers while retaining engine, component and zero-emissions pathways; this multi-technology position provides resilience if the pace of powertrain transition differs across end markets.

Data-center growth increases demand for power-generation equipment, but the successor bottlenecks are grid availability, generator supply chains, permitting/emissions constraints and customer buildout timing rather than generator technology alone.

risks.risk: Data-center power growth can be strong while truck/off-highway cycles weaken other Cummins segments.

unknowns.unknown: Current disclosures do not isolate data-center backlog economics or customer concentration.

claims.claim: Q2 2026 Power Systems sales rose 19% with data-center demand a major driver, while Accelera still posted a $69M EBITDA loss; growth therefore coexists with transition investment drag rather than proving uniformly improving economics.

Cummins reports firm orders from data-center and electrolyzer customers but also states a large portion of its business uses open purchase orders cancellable on reasonable notice, so broad backlog language should not be treated as uniformly firm demand.

causalEdges: Accelera investment -> near-term EBITDA drag -> transition optionality

risks.risk: Open-order cancellability makes some demand less durable than headline backlog language may imply.
Zero-emissions investments remain loss-making and require disciplined pacing.

contradictions.contradiction: Record/strong revenue growth coexists with lower consolidated year-over-year EBITDA margin and continued Accelera losses.

unknowns.unknown: Incremental margins and concentration of data-center power-generation demand are not separately disclosed.
